title: Fine-tuned atomistic foundation model for accurate sodium-carbon chemistry in Na-ion batteries
authors: Andres Felipe Usuga (Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o)
Ihor Radchenko (Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o)
College of Chemical Engineering - Fuzhou University)
Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o)
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18490v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. Hard carbon features diverse local structural motifs, including defective and curved graphitic regions, amorphous regions, and closed/open pores. Motivated by its importance for Na-ion batteries, we systematically evaluate existing pretrained foundation models based on the MACE architecture across different local Na/C motifs. We find that the pretrained models fail to accurately capture Na-Na and Na-C interactions for metallic Na clusters on graphene. To recover a DFT-level energetic description, we employ targeted fine-tuning, showing that it can describe the energetic stability of local motifs and achieve sufficient transferability to unseen Na/C environments. With the developed fine-tuned model, we establish a correlation between closed-pore radius in hard carbon and plateau voltage, showing that the small pores contribute at larger voltages than large ones, suggesting thus how the developed fine-tuned foundation model can link atomistic information with materials design for complex bonding environments.
relevance_reason: Targeted fine-tuning and benchmarking of MACE-based atomistic foundation models for Na/C motifs plus derived pore-voltage relations; clear MLIP development and application satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: Electric Fields Turn Vacancy-trapping Grain Boundaries into Li-Ion Pathways in Li2O
abstract:
arXiv:2611.17679v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ion transport in solids has conventionally been understood from equilibrium diffusion, yet ions in batteries are driven by electric fields. Does field-driven ion transport follow equilibrium behavior? We examined this question in bulk Li2O and at its grain boundaries (GBs) using electric-field molecular dynamics combining a machine learning interatomic potential with a Bader charge prediction model. Although Li diffusion in cubic Li2O is isotropic at zero field, an electric field renders it orientation dependent because Li hops along a limited set of crystallographic pathways that the field biases unequally. At GBs, this anisotropy becomes a qualitative difference: a GB that strongly traps Li vacancies but exhibits a strong field response releases them under a field, whereas a weakly responsive GB retains them despite weaker vacancy trapping. These results show that field-driven GB transport is governed not by static thermodynamics alone but by the angle between the electric field and the diffusion pathways of the constituent grains.
relevance_reason: The paper performs electric-field molecular dynamics with a machine-learned interatomic potential and Bader charge prediction, clearly satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD/MLIP methodology, and (c) application to Li-ion transport in Li2O grain boundaries.

title: A Practical Route to Demonstrating Core Reactivity in Cs Polyoxides under Pressure
abstract:
arXiv:2110.07865v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Activating normally inert core electrons expands the bonding possibilities of elements beyond conventional valence chemistry. Although Cs core reactivity under pressure was predicted in polyfluorides more than a decade ago, experimental confirmation remains elusive, largely because loading highly corrosive F$_{2}$ poses serious challenges for diamond anvil cells. Here, global crystal structure searches combined with first-principles calculations identify Cs polyoxides as a practical alternative for investigating core reactivity. Compression activates Cs 5p electrons, leading to oxidation beyond the usual +1 state and a striking reversal of conventional polyoxide behavior: O-O bonds disappear, while strong Cs-O covalent bonds generate molecular units and extended sheets. Most importantly, CsO, a solid peroxide stable at ambient pressure, is predicted to undergo this transformation at 221 GPa, forming linear [CsO$_{2}$]$^{-}$ units. This approach replaces a chemical reaction between separate reactants with a phase transition in a single solid, avoiding F$_{2}$ loading and simplifying experimental implementation without changing the overall composition. The loss of peroxide O-O pairs provides a vibrational signature of the transformation, while calculated infrared and Cs L$_{3}$-edge XANES spectra, together with simulated X-ray diffraction patterns, guide experimental identification. These results establish an experimentally testable route toward core reactivity and show how pressure can extend the chemical possibilities of a familiar alkali metal.
relevance_reason: Uses global crystal structure searches combined with first-principles DFT calculations on explicit atomic structures under pressure, satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18041v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One of the defining characteristics of most energy materials, used as e.g.~battery electrodes, photovoltaics, or photocatalysts, is their ability conduct charges such as electrons and holes. The exact mechanism of this conductivity depends on the material, but is often dominated by the existence of mobile small polarons, i.e.~electrons or holes strongly localised through the polarisation of their environment. Computationally, small polarons can be treated with reasonably accuracy through the use of self-interaction corrected or hybrid density functional theory (DFT) together with local geometry optimisation. Similar approaches can be employed to determine the energy barriers to movement of the polarons through hopping. Unfortunately, realistic energy materials tend have very large numbers of symmetry inequivalent polaronic configurations and correspondingly large numbers of hopping barriers, making them hard to tackle explicitly.
  In this work we therefore extend the computational reach of DFT calculations with machine-learned (ML) surrogate models, which then feed into a kinetic model to quantitatively estimate the conductivity of a battery anode material (Li$_4$Ti$_5$O$_12$ or LTO) at realistic, defected conditions. We calculate the conductivity at room temperature to be 6.7 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ S/cm which lies well in the experimental range. To this end, we only needed a total of 154 polaron barrier calculations, out of 3649 symmetry inequivalent ones, achieving an over 20-fold increase of computational efficiency. Overall, our work demonstrates how DFT-trained ML surrogates can be used to quantitatively and efficiently sample the dynamics of small polarons in energy materials.
relevance_reason: The paper uses DFT polaron barrier calculations, local geometry optimization, and ML surrogate models feeding a kinetic transport model, satisfying (a) explicit atomic configurations, (b) DFT/geometry-optimization-based atomistic simulation, and (c) application to small-polaron dynamics in an energy material.

title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18161v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. We analyze their structural motifs, stability, and electronic band structures, highlighting recurring prototype families, several of which show intrinsic intermediate-band features. Our results substantially expand the known phase space of cubic chiral semiconductors and may guide future efforts in the discovery and design of chiral materials.
relevance_reason: High-throughput DFT (convex-hull stability, band structures) combined with ML for crystal structure discovery in space group P4_332; explicit atomistic DFT calculations satisfy (a), (b), and (c).

title: Ultralow Lattice Thermal Conductivity in Orthorhombic Rb2Se3 with rigid covalent trimers and a soft ionic framework
abstract:
arXiv:2507.21634v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Alkali-metal-containing compounds often exhibit exceptionally low lattice thermal conductivity, yet the structural origins and transport mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate orthorhombic Rb2Se3 using first-principles bonding, lattice-dynamical, and thermal-transport calculations. Bonding analyses reveal strongly covalent, V-shaped Se3 trimers embedded in a soft ionic coordination framework. Representing each trimer as a pseudo-atom reveals a pseudo-one-dimensional chain arrangement along [001] within the three-dimensional crystal.This bonding hierarchy produces a dense low-frequency phonon manifold and four separated high-frequency optical branches dominated by internal trimer stretching. Four-phonon scattering strongly suppresses particle-like heat transport, leaving the coherent contribution dominant. The coherent contribution is largest along the pseudo-atom-chain direction [001] and accounts for most of the thermal conductivity anisotropy. At 300 K, the total lattice thermal conductivities are 0.067, 0.096, and 0.265 W/mK along [100], [010], and [001], respectively. These results connect the coexistence of rigid covalent trimers and a soft ionic framework to ultra-low thermal conductivity, while revealing how their structural arrangement is reflected in directional coherent heat transfer.
relevance_reason: Applies first-principles DFT, bonding analysis, lattice dynamics, and thermal-transport calculations to an explicit atomic crystal, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Intrinsic Defect Energetics and Fluorine Doping Effects in Li2CO3 and Li2O2: A First-Principles Study
abstract:
arXiv:2606.25408v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Lithium carbonate, Li2CO3, is a thermodynamically stable carbonate phase whose defect energetics are closely related to its stability and decomposition behavior in various lithium-based electrochemical systems. These properties of Li2CO3 are particularly important in lithium-oxygen battery environments. In these systems, Li2CO3 can form as a parasitic discharge product alongside Li2O2, the primary discharge product, leading to performance degradation. However, compared with Li2O2, the intrinsic defect thermodynamics of Li2CO3 and how chemical doping modifies its defect energetics remain insufficiently understood. In this study, first-principles calculations were performed to systematically analyze the intrinsic point-defect energetics of Li2CO3 and to evaluate the effects of fluorine doping on vacancy formation energies in Li2CO3 and Li2O2. Intrinsic defect analysis reveals that defect behavior is predominantly governed by lithium-related defects. Upon fluorine doping, lithium and carbon vacancy formation energies decrease selectively in Li2CO3, partially destabilizing the carbonate framework, while a reduction in lithium vacancy formation energy is also observed in Li2O2. These results suggest that fluorine doping modulates the defect energetics of both discharge products, potentially providing a thermodynamic basis for controlling the stability of Li2CO3 and Li2O2 under thermodynamic conditions representative of lithium-oxygen batteries.
relevance_reason: Performs first-principles DFT calculations of point-defect energetics and doping effects in explicit Li2CO3/Li2O2 atomic structures, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
abstract: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods. We compared the wild-type (WT) lectin domain (PDB 4XO8, apo) with R60P, Y137A and Q133K, using three 500 ns molecular dynamics (MD) replicates per system (6 microseconds total) and three folding-stability predictors (FoldX, a Cartesian-ddG-type Rosetta protocol, ERIS-2). The replicate was the unit of analysis (n = 3), with 95% confidence intervals and a WT replicate-to-replicate control. Results. FoldX and ERIS-2 ranked the variants consistently, R60P most destabilising and Q133K neutral; the Rosetta value for Q133K was anomalously high. All systems stayed folded. R60P gave the only reproduced local change, loss of beta-strand structure at residues 60-61 and of three local hydrogen bonds. Y137A did not bring Thr158 into the pocket, and the Q133K Gln133-Asp54 polar contact became a Lys133-Asp54 salt bridge. In the principal-component landscape, departures from the WT region came from individual replicates (Y137A replicate 1; Q133K replicates 2-3), not a systematic shift. Conclusions. A substitution perturbs local structure most clearly when it breaks a beta-strand (R60P), and the stability predictions and dynamics together give a consistent ranking of the variants, including the first dynamic characterisation of Q133K. The results characterise the apo lectin domain and give a reproducible basis for interpreting FimH mutations, not for inferring affinity. Keywords: FimH; lectin domain; point mutations; molecular dynamics; folding stability ({Delta}{Delta}G); protein stability prediction; principal component analysis; urinary tract infection.
relevance_reason: Runs three 500 ns classical all-atom MD replicates per FimH lectin-domain variant (6 microseconds total) plus FoldX/Rosetta/ERIS-2 stability prediction, so explicit atoms (a), molecular dynamics (b), and application to mutant conformational dynamics (c) are all satisfied.

title: Compression of virtual spaces in transcorrelated methods via singular value decomposition: application to the G2 set
abstract:
arXiv:2608.10658v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce a new singular-value-decomposition-based scheme for constructing small virtual spaces out of large basis sets for transcorrelated (TC) calculations, termed SVD-TC. This work builds on the recent finding that the residual basis error in the TC reference energy converges more slowly than that of the correlation energy. Within the new workflow, the post Hartree-Fock TC calculation is performed in a compressed virtual orbital subspace, obtained by projecting the canonical virtual orbitals from a large basis set onto a smaller basis set through singular value decomposition (SVD). This allows us to achieve the high accuracy allowed by the large basis, whilst the bottleneck steps - TC integral calculation and post-HF correlation method such as CCSD(T) - incur the cost of only a small virtual space calculation. The method therefore is highly efficient, whilst avoiding the composite nature of the reference correction method. Using the new scheme, we widen the scope of benchmark-quality TC results into more complex molecules than previously considered: using the G2-1 set of 55 molecules with first- and second-row atoms, we apply SVD-xTC-CCSD(T) to compute atomization energies. We compare our results against the near-exact semistochastic heat-bath configuration interaction (SHCI) reference values and experiment. We find that SVD-xTC-CCSD(T) delivers chemical accuracy already with triple-$\zeta$ basis sets. Finally, we use the quadruple-$\zeta$ results to analyze the accuracy of pseudopotentials within the TC method, and show that pseudopotential TC workflow provides faster basis-set convergence than all-electron TC. We also present timings for computing the atomization energies on G2-1 set, demonstrating the efficiency of our TC workflows.
relevance_reason: Develops an SVD virtual-space compression scheme for transcorrelated CCSD(T) applied to atomization energies of explicit molecules, satisfying (a) and (b) via post-Hartree-Fock electronic structure and advancing the method (c).

title: Uniaxial strain induces $d$-wave phonon chirality in ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18402v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Circularly dichroic resonant inelastic x-ray scattering has revealed electrically switchable $g$-wave phonon chirality in freestanding BaTiO$_3$ membranes. Here, we show from first principles that uniaxial strain changes the angular class of this texture. Lowering $C_{4v}$ to $C_{2v}$ adds a $d$-wave helicity that is bilinear in the orthorhombic strain $\eta$ and the polarization, with nodal lines along the stress axis. For the 38~meV branches at $\eta=1\%$, we find that (i) along the diagonal, where the helicity vanishes by symmetry without strain, it reaches about 60\% of the unstrained maximum, and (ii) at the measured wave vectors off the mirror it is reduced by more than half. With PBEsol and PBE+D3 force constants, the $d$-wave component grows linearly in $\eta$ and equals the $g$-wave one at $\eta^*\approx1.3\text{--}1.4\%$. Resolved by branch, the response of strain-split $E$ doublets is non-analytic in $\eta$, as captured by a two-band model. Strain therefore provides a second knob, besides the electric field, that controls the symmetry and the sign of phonon chirality in ferroelectric membranes.
relevance_reason: First-principles (PBEsol, PBE+D3) force-constant and phonon calculations on BaTiO3 under strain; explicit atoms plus DFT satisfies (a)-(c), though it is a DFT application rather than a simulation-method advance.

title: Drumhead Surface States of Rhombohedral Graphite with Near Ideal Quantum Geometry Condition
abstract:
arXiv:2607.28491v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The ideal quantum geometry (IQG) condition for the trace of quantum metric ($TrG(k)$) being equal to the magnitude of Berry curvature (|$\Omega(k)$|) as in $|\Omega|$/Tr$G$=1 has been associated with realizing fractional Chern insulators for the flat bands in a few layers of rhombohedral graphene (RG). More recently the IQG condition has also been proposed for superconductivity in the flat bands of thick RG layers. Using density functional theory and Wannier functions, we study the symmetry-protected topology of bulk RG, drumhead surface states (DSS) of semi-infinite RG surface and slabs, and the IQG condition for thin and thick RG slabs. We find that bulk RG is a weak topological insulator with spin-orbit coupling (SOC), besides being effectively a chiral semimetal with chiral nodal lines without SOC. We also find that the DSS flat bands of thick RG slabs have a sizable convex curvature with dispersion depth agreeing with the recent angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy experiment. The calculated IQG also shows a convex shape with the K point at the center having a minimum with approximately $|\Omega|$/Tr$G$$\approx$1. But the inner rim of the DSS region approaches the IQG condition of $|\Omega|$/Tr$G$=1. These results on thick RG slabs from first-principles calculations provide useful information for the pristine DSS at the single-particle level for future studies to consider when enhanced electron correlation and many-body interaction will be included.
relevance_reason: Uses DFT and Wannier functions to study electronic topology in explicit rhombohedral graphite atomic structures, satisfying (a)-(c) through first-principles atomistic calculations.

title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13736v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate intrinsic color centers in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation {\Delta}SCF calcula-tions identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. Com-paring their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It has the high-est calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate (43.9 MHz) and ZPL quantum efficiency (11.8%) among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation gives a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a mul-timode photoluminescence calculation predicts a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37% and a dominant zero-phonon contribution. Its predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) is also closest in photon energy to the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets. Quantum frequency upconversion could connect this strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands, providing a route toward fiber-based quantum communication with an intrinsic color center.
relevance_reason: Uses hybrid DFT and constrained-occupation Delta-SCF calculations on explicit divacancy defects in hexagonal diamond, satisfying (a)-(c) as a first-principles defect study.
